title: Prospect Theory in Large Language Models: A Meta-Analysis of Loss Aversion, Diminishing Sensitivity, and Probability Weighting
abstract: arXiv:2610.33103v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Prospect theory splits risky choice into three parts: loss aversion, measured by the relative weight of losses to gains, $\lambda$ (e.g., $\lambda = 2$ implies that losses weigh twice as much as gains), diminishing sensitivity to the size of outcomes (i.e., the curvature and linearity of the value function), and the nonlinear weighting of probabilities. I examined whether Large Language Models (LLMs) display the same properties as people by meta-analyzing 102 fitted estimates from 11 studies covering 32 language models. The three components emerge differently. Loss aversion is modest: the pooled $\lambda$ is 1.26 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.46), far below the strongest human meta-analytic estimate ($\lambda = 1.96$) and compatible with more conservative ones (1.07 and 1.31). Matched by design, LLMs are compatible with people when gains and losses are symmetric ($\lambda = 1.15$ against 1.07), but well below them when losses are smaller than gains

translated_title: 大型语言模型中的前景理论：对损失厌恶、敏感性递减与概率加权的元分析
translated_abstract: 前景理论将风险决策分解为三个部分：损失厌恶（以损失相对于收益的权重λ来衡量，例如λ=2意味着损失的权重是收益的两倍）、对结果大小的敏感性递减（即价值函数的曲率与线性特征），以及概率的非线性加权。本文通过对涵盖32个语言模型的11项研究中的102个拟合估计进行元分析，考察大型语言模型（LLM）是否表现出与人类相同的特性。研究发现这三个组成部分的表现各不相同：LLM的损失厌恶程度较为温和，汇总后的λ为1.26（95%置信区间为1.06至1.46），远低于最强的人类元分析估计值（λ=1.96），但与较为保守的人类估计值（1.07和1.31）相容。在匹配设计下，当收益与损失对称时，LLM与人类表现相容（λ=1.15对1.07），但当损失小于收益时，LLM的损失厌恶程度则远低于人类。
tldr: 本文通过对32个语言模型的102个拟合估计进行元分析，发现大型语言模型表现出温和的损失厌恶（λ=1.26）：在收益与损失对称情境下其行为与人类相容，但总体损失厌恶程度显著低于人类，且三个前景理论成分的表现各不相同。
en_tdlr: This meta-analysis of 102 fitted estimates from 32 language models reveals that LLMs exhibit modest loss aversion (λ=1.26)—compatible with humans in symmetric gain-loss contexts but substantially weaker overall—and that the three components of prospect theory emerge differently in LLMs than in people.
